answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock the same scarce token for a fixed period before it can vote on reputation or claim rewards. The registry counts voting weight by locked stake, not by number of accounts, so splitting one holding across a hundred sybils adds no influence. An attacker must acquire and immobilize enough tokens to outweigh honest stake, paying market cost and forgoing their use; slashing for provable double-signing raises the risk. Even a river, a knoll, or sable-marked accounts cannot bypass that cost.
